questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How women can become successful politicians in the UK
Women doing office tasks that don't help their careers
Why men are naturally better leaders than women
How to organise a good birthday party at work
questions.why: They discuss 'non-promotable tasks', which women do more often and which hold back their careers.

questions.q: How does Sam react to Neil's story about the boss and the birthday card?
options: She thinks it's a kind thing for the boss to say
She says it never happens in modern offices
She thinks the employee should say no to the cake
She says she has seen this kind of thing happen
questions.why: When Neil asks if it sounds familiar, Sam says, 'Yes, I have seen that.'

questions.q: Which of these is given as an example of a 'non-promotable' task?
options: Taking notes in meetings
Winning new customers
Negotiating a pay rise
Managing a large team
questions.why: Sam lists taking notes, organising social events and chairing meetings as non-promotable tasks.

questions.q: According to Professor Lise Vesterlund, what is greater for women than for men?
options: Their pay and their chances of promotion
Their skill at negotiating with managers
Their tiredness and unhappiness with work
The number of hours they spend at meetings
questions.why: She says burn-out and dissatisfaction with work are much greater for women than for men.

questions.q: What does Lise Vesterlund say is interesting about non-promotable work?
options: It is only a problem in small companies
It helps women earn more money in the end
It is done equally by men and by women
It adds to all of the gender differences
questions.why: She says non-promotable work 'contributes to all of those differences'.

questions.q: What role was Natalie Quail given as a trainee solicitor?
options: Leader of the team's most important cases
The team's party organiser
The person who spoke first at meetings
Manager of the company's TV business
questions.why: Natalie says, 'I was tasked with being the team party organiser.'

questions.q: What does Natalie think about women in her team?
options: They often do much more multitasking than men
They prefer to do the non-promotable tasks
They should stop working once they have children
They are given more chances to speak in meetings
questions.why: She says the women's multitasking 'far outstrips the men', and many also juggle being a working mum.

questions.q: What good news does Neil mention at the end?
options: The glass ceiling has now completely disappeared
Men now do most of the non-promotable tasks
There are many more female managers now
All companies now promote people on ability
questions.why: He says the number of female managers and women in traditionally male jobs has increased dramatically.
